# Question

A deviation model of `weather_arms_robustness.Rmd` (PWT x ERA5) applied to the
stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) seed ensemble of `data/Scenarios`: the
GDP each country, and the world, loses to the temperature and precipitation of
each scenario, net of the growth effect of natural variability alone, with the
uncertainty of the coefficients and of natural variability.

The functions are in `functions/scenario_projection.R`; the models are those
saved by `weather_arms_robustness.Rmd` (knit it first), and the parameters
`definition` and `form` pick one. Choices of this notebook:

- the model: `r params$form`, with `r params$definition` deviations, each
  interacted with the horizon mean;
- the 20-year deviations are measured against the scenario's own trailing
  20-year mean, in a fixed SD: the country's ERA5 trailing 20-year SD (median
  over its estimation years) with the `baseline` parameter `fixed_sd`; the
  alternatives are the scenario's own trailing SD (`moving`), or both moments
  held through each run of rising (falling) years (`runs`); here:
  `r params$baseline`. The horizon deviations are measured against the ERA5
  moments of the model, with the scenario climate as it is (no bias
  correction);
- the model is applied as estimated, and, as a variant, with each arm capped at
  its largest deviation in the estimation sample;
- losses accumulate from `r params$start_year`;
- uncertainty: `r params$n_draws` draws of the coefficients, each applied to
  every seed, pooled.

# Setup

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
source("load_functions.R")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

START <- as.integer(params$start_year)
PROBS <- c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95)
COUNTRY_YEARS <- c(2050L, 2100L, 2150L)
WORKERS <- if (identical(params$workers, "auto")) {
  max(1L, min(12L, parallel::detectCores() - 2L))
} else {
  as.integer(params$workers)
}

model <- load_preferred_model(params$definition, params$form)
draws <- coefficient_draws(model, n = as.integer(params$n_draws))
scenarios <- scenario_matrix()
ds <- scenario_dataset()
```

Model: **`r model$form`**, **`r model$definition`** deviations, `r model$panel`,
`r model$observations` country-years, horizon `r model$horizon[1]`-`r model$horizon[2]`;
AIC `r sprintf("%+.1f", model$aic_vs_best)` against the best saved model (the
preferred one of `weather_arms_robustness.Rmd` is `r model$preferred[["form"]]`,
`r model$preferred[["definition"]]` deviations).

# The scenarios

`data/Scenarios/sai_seed_country_global_timeseries.parquet` (see its README):
`r nrow(scenarios)` scenarios, annual 1990-2150, for 131 countries, the
residual region ROW and WORLD. Each scenario is an RCP, an SAI setting and a
seed of natural variability:

```{r scenario-matrix}
scenarios %>%
  mutate(rcp = factor(scenario_rcp_label(rcp), levels = unname(SCENARIO_RCPS)),
         term = factor(scenario_term_label(term), levels = scenario_term_label(SCENARIO_TERMS))) %>%
  count(term, rcp) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = rcp, values_from = n) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Scenarios: seeds by SAI setting (rows) and RCP (columns)")
```

The SAI settings include a termination in 2040 besides 2050-2100; all are
projected. The variables used:

| Column | Here | Content |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `temperature_deg_c` | T | country temperature (C) |
| `precipitation_lt_per_yr` | P | country precipitation; labelled lt/yr in the source, in metres a year (as RR of the model, see below) |
| `DTEMP_REGION_VAR`, `DPRECIP_REGION_VAR` | TVAR, PVAR | natural-variability components of T and P, from 2015 |
| `ykali_trillion_2005_usd_ppp` | GDP | GDP of the scenario (trillion 2005 USD PPP) |
| `population_million` | POP | population (million) |
| `TATM_VAR` | | variability of the global temperature (WORLD only) |

## Checks

```{r scenario-checks}
exogenous <- ds %>%
  group_by(region, year) %>%
  summarise(gdp = max(ykali_trillion_2005_usd_ppp) / min(ykali_trillion_2005_usd_ppp) - 1,
            pop = max(population_million) / min(population_million) - 1) %>%
  quiet_collect()
variability <- ds %>%
  filter(year >= 2015L, region_type == "country") %>%
  group_by(seed, region, year) %>%
  summarise(T = max(DTEMP_REGION_VAR) - min(DTEMP_REGION_VAR),
            P = max(DPRECIP_REGION_VAR) - min(DPRECIP_REGION_VAR)) %>%
  quiet_collect()
historical <- ds %>%
  filter(year < 2015L, region_type == "country") %>%
  group_by(region, year) %>%
  summarise(T = max(temperature_deg_c) - min(temperature_deg_c),
            P = max(precipitation_lt_per_yr) - min(precipitation_lt_per_yr),
            variability = sum(if_else(is.na(DTEMP_REGION_VAR), 0L, 1L))) %>%
  quiet_collect()
forced <- ds %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2050L, 2100L), region_type == "country") %>%
  mutate(forced = temperature_deg_c - DTEMP_REGION_VAR) %>%
  group_by(rcp, term, region, year) %>%
  summarise(sd = sd(forced)) %>%
  quiet_collect()
negative <- ds %>%
  filter(region_type == "country") %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(rows = n(),
            negative = sum(if_else(precipitation_lt_per_yr < 0, 1L, 0L)),
            negative_forced = sum(if_else(precipitation_lt_per_yr - DPRECIP_REGION_VAR < 0, 1L, 0L),
                                  na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_P = mean(precipitation_lt_per_yr)) %>%
  quiet_collect() %>%
  filter(negative > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(negative))

tibble::tribble(
  ~check, ~result,
  "GDP and population: largest relative difference across the scenarios",
  sprintf("%.1e and %.1e", max(exogenous$gdp), max(exogenous$pop)),
  "Natural variability (from 2015): largest difference across RCPs and SAI settings within a seed",
  sprintf("%.1e C and %.1e m", max(variability$T), max(variability$P)),
  "1990-2014 climate: largest difference across scenarios; natural variability in those years",
  sprintf("%.1e C and %.1e m; %d rows", max(historical$T), max(historical$P), sum(historical$variability)),
  "T without natural variability (T - TVAR): SD across the 10 seeds in 2050 and 2100, median over countries and RCPs, without SAI",
  with(forced[forced$term == "BASE", ], sprintf("%.3f and %.3f C", stats::median(sd[year == 2050]),
                                                 stats::median(sd[year == 2100]))),
  "The same with SAI (never terminated or terminated in any year)",
  with(forced[forced$term != "BASE", ], sprintf("%.3f and %.3f C", stats::median(sd[year == 2050]),
                                                 stats::median(sd[year == 2100]))),
  "Country-years with negative precipitation, all scenarios (countries)",
  sprintf("%d (%d)", sum(negative$negative), nrow(negative))
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Checks of the scenario data")
```

GDP and population are the same in every scenario: they are the exogenous
paths, so the per-capita growth `dlog(GDP / POP)` is the same in every
scenario and the climate enters only through the model. The natural
variability of a seed is the same in every RCP and SAI setting, so the
scenarios of a seed differ only in the rest of their climate. Without SAI that
rest (T - TVAR) also differs across the seeds (by about 0.2 C), so part of the
seed-to-seed variation is not in TVAR and is not netted out by g(TVAR, PVAR);
with SAI, even after termination, it is practically the same in every seed.
Before 2015 every scenario has the same climate and no variability component.

```{r negative-precipitation}
negative %>%
  mutate(country = countrycode::countrycode(region, "iso3c", "country.name", warn = FALSE),
         share = round(negative / rows, 3), mean_P = round(mean_P, 3)) %>%
  select(country, country_years = rows, negative, share, negative_forced, mean_P) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Country-years with negative precipitation (all scenarios; negative_forced:",
                               "P - PVAR < 0; mean_P in m a year). They are kept as they are."))
```

## Natural variability and the historical climate against ERA5

The model measures deviations in each country's ERA5 SD over
`r model$horizon[1]`-`r model$horizon[2]` (which includes the trend). The
natural variability of the scenarios, against ERA5:

```{r variability-era5}
era5 <- load_climate_series("gadm0", panel_config(
  econ_year_min = model$horizon[[1]], climate_source = "ERA5",
  climate_weight = "population density", climate_weight_year = 2000L
)) %>%
  filter(year >= model$horizon[[1]], year <= model$horizon[[2]]) %>%
  transmute(region = GID_0, year, TM, RR)
detrended_sd <- function(x, year) stats::sd(stats::resid(stats::lm(x ~ poly(year, 2))))
observed <- era5 %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(T_detrended = detrended_sd(TM, year), P_detrended = detrended_sd(RR, year),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  inner_join(model$moments, by = c(region = "GID_0"))
simulated <- ds %>%
  filter(rcp == "RCP45", term == "BASE", year >= 2015L, region_type == "country") %>%
  select(seed, region, year, TVAR = DTEMP_REGION_VAR, PVAR = DPRECIP_REGION_VAR) %>%
  quiet_collect() %>%
  arrange(region, seed, year) %>%
  group_by(region, seed) %>%
  mutate(T_ar1 = stats::cor(TVAR[-1], TVAR[-n()])) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(T_sd = stats::sd(TVAR), P_sd = stats::sd(PVAR), T_mean = mean(TVAR),
            P_mean = mean(PVAR), T_ar1 = stats::median(T_ar1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  inner_join(observed, by = "region")

quartiles <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", stats::median(x), stats::quantile(x, 0.25),
                                 stats::quantile(x, 0.75))
tibble::tribble(
  ~statistic, ~temperature, ~precipitation,
  "SD of the variability / SD of ERA5 around its quadratic trend",
  quartiles(simulated$T_sd / simulated$T_detrended), quartiles(simulated$P_sd / simulated$P_detrended),
  "SD of the variability / ERA5 horizon SD (the SD of d_var)",
  quartiles(simulated$T_sd / simulated$sd_TM_all), quartiles(simulated$P_sd / simulated$sd_RR_all),
  "Mean of the variability (C, m)",
  quartiles(simulated$T_mean), quartiles(simulated$P_mean),
  "First-order autocorrelation of the variability",
  quartiles(simulated$T_ar1), ""
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Natural variability of the scenarios (2015-2150, RCP4.5 without SAI,",
                               "the 10 seeds) against ERA5: median [quartiles] over countries"))

scenario_history <- ds %>%
  filter(scenario == !!scenarios$scenario[[1]], year < 2015L, region_type == "country") %>%
  select(region, year, T = temperature_deg_c, P = precipitation_lt_per_yr) %>%
  quiet_collect()
gap <- scenario_history %>%
  inner_join(era5, by = c("region", "year")) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(T_gap = mean(T - TM), P_gap = mean(P - RR), P_ratio = mean(P) / mean(RR),
            T_cor = stats::cor(T, TM), P_cor = stats::cor(P, RR), .groups = "drop") %>%
  inner_join(model$moments, by = c(region = "GID_0")) %>%
  mutate(T_gap_sd = T_gap / sd_TM_all, P_gap_sd = P_gap / sd_RR_all)
tibble::tribble(
  ~statistic, ~temperature, ~precipitation,
  "Mean gap, scenario - ERA5 (C, m)", quartiles(gap$T_gap), quartiles(gap$P_gap),
  "Mean gap in ERA5 horizon SDs", quartiles(gap$T_gap_sd), quartiles(gap$P_gap_sd),
  "Absolute gap in SDs, 90th percentile and largest",
  sprintf("%.2f and %.2f", stats::quantile(abs(gap$T_gap_sd), 0.9), max(abs(gap$T_gap_sd))),
  sprintf("%.2f and %.2f", stats::quantile(abs(gap$P_gap_sd), 0.9), max(abs(gap$P_gap_sd))),
  "Ratio of the means, scenario / ERA5", "", quartiles(gap$P_ratio),
  "Year-to-year correlation", quartiles(gap$T_cor), quartiles(gap$P_cor)
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("The 1990-2014 climate of the scenarios against ERA5 (the same in every",
                               "scenario): median [quartiles] over countries"))
```

The precipitation of the scenarios has the level of ERA5 in metres a year, so
it is used as RR without conversion. The 1990-2014 climate of the scenarios is
model output (it does not follow the observed years) and differs in level
from ERA5. With horizon deviations (against the ERA5 mean, no bias
correction) that gap enters every deviation; the 20-year deviations are
measured against the scenario's own trailing mean, so it does not.

# From the estimated model to GDP losses

**What was estimated** (PWT x ERA5, country-years `r model$horizon[1]`-`r model$horizon[2]`):

```text
dlog y_it = sum_v sum_arm (a_v,arm + b_v,arm m_v,i) f_arm(d_v,it) + controls + FE + e
horizon:  d_v,it = (X_v,it - m_v,i) / s_v,i            m, s: the country's ERA5 mean and SD over the horizon
20-year:  d_v,it = (X_v,it - mean20_v,it) / sd20_v,it   mean and SD of the 20 years before t
f         temperature: (d+)^2, (d-)^2; precipitation: d+, d-   (d+ = max(d, 0), d- = max(-d, 0))
```

X_T is temperature and X_P precipitation; every interaction is with the
horizon mean m. In the estimation, d was demeaned (each country's mean and
quadratic trend removed) before the arms were cut; in the projections d is the
deviation itself, as in the warming scenario of `weather_arms_robustness.Rmd`
(demeaning would remove the warming).

**Growth effect** in scenario s, country i, year t, with the scenario's T and P
as they are (here: `r model$definition` deviations):

```text
horizon:                    d = (X_s,it - m_i) / s_i          d_var = VAR_s,it / s_i
20-year:                    d = (X_s,it - mean20(X)) / s20    d_var = (VAR_s,it - mean20(VAR)) / s20
20-year mean, horizon SD:   d = (X_s,it - mean20(X)) / s_i    d_var = (VAR_s,it - mean20(VAR)) / s_i
g(T, P)       = sum (a + b m) f(d)
g(TVAR, PVAR) = sum (a + b m) f(d_var)
dg_s,it       = g(T, P) - g(TVAR, PVAR)
```

mean20 is the mean of the scenario's own series over t-20..t-1 (the
1990-2014 history included); that of the natural variability alone, the
counterfactual, which starts in 2015, comes from the years of the window with
it, at least `r VARIABILITY_MIN_YEARS` (from 2025). s20, with the 20-year
deviations, depends on the `baseline` parameter:

- `fixed_sd` (the default): the country's ERA5 trailing 20-year SD, median
  over its estimation years, in both terms;
- `moving`: the SD of the scenario's own series over t-20..t-1 (of the
  variability alone for d_var), so it moves with the scenario: a fast warming
  widens it and shrinks the deviations;
- `runs`: the trailing mean and SD held through each warming (cooling) run,
  the consecutive years each warmer (cooler) than the one before, at the last
  year before the run, as the run-fixed deviations of
  `weather_arms_robustness.Rmd`: the run ends with the first year that is not
  warmer (cooler) than the one before, and the warm (wet) arm is cut from the
  warming (wetting) runs, the cold (dry) arm from the cooling (drying) ones; a
  run whose first year has no moments yet keeps the moving ones; the
  counterfactual alike, through its own runs;
- `sigma_spells`: the same, held through spells that end only with a
  reversal larger than the held SD or with the third consecutive smaller one
  (`fix_sigma_spells()` in `functions/climate_runs.R`, as in the one-SD spell
  section of `weather_arms_robustness.Rmd`).

The coefficients are those of the model estimated with the moving 20-year
moments (or with the horizon SD, for that definition). The fixed effects and
controls belong to the baseline, so they do not enter dg.

**From growth to GDP.** The per-capita growth of the scenario is that of its
GDP and population, `g_t = dlog(GDP_t / POP_t)`; with the climate it is
`g_t + dg_t` from `r START`. So, from `r START` to t,

```text
log y^cc_t - log y_t = L_t = sum_{tau = START..t} dg_tau
GDP^cc_t = GDP_t exp(L_t)                         (population unchanged)
loss_i,t = 1 - exp(L_i,t)                         (share of the scenario's GDP)
loss_R,t = 1 - sum_R GDP_i,t exp(L_i,t) / sum_R GDP_i,t    for countries R (all, or a subset)
```

ROW has no observed climate and is left out of every aggregate (about 2% of
world GDP).

**Uncertainty.** L_i,t = c_i,t' beta, with c_i,t the sum over the years of the
difference of the two design rows, is linear in the 8 weather coefficients.
Each of `r params$n_draws` draws beta^(k) ~ N(beta, VCOV clustered by country)
is applied to each of the 10 seeds; the bands are the
`r 100 * PROBS[1]`-`r 100 * PROBS[3]`% quantiles of the pooled 10 x
`r params$n_draws` values (every `r params$draw_step` years, the draws costing
one exp() per country, year and draw), the central line their median, and the
thin lines the point estimate of each seed (every year).

**Capped variant.** Each arm's |d| is capped at its largest value in the
estimation sample (temperature +`r round(max(model$support$TM), 2)` and
`r round(min(model$support$TM), 2)` SD, precipitation
+`r round(max(model$support$RR), 2)` and `r round(min(model$support$RR), 2)`
SD), in both terms of dg: beyond it the effect stays at its value at the
largest deviation observed.

```{r model-coefficients}
tibble::tibble(term = names(model$coef), estimate = model$coef,
               std_error = sqrt(diag(model$vcov))) %>%
  mutate(across(c(estimate, std_error), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Weather coefficients of the preferred model (errors clustered by",
                               "country); the controls and fixed effects are not used"))

# Growth effect that year of a deviation d at long-run climate m, as estimated
# and capped, to show how far the projections extrapolate.
effect_grid <- function(v, d, m) {
  grid <- expand.grid(d = d, m = m)
  zero <- rep(0, nrow(grid))
  dev <- if (v == "TM") list(TM = grid$d, RR = zero) else list(TM = zero, RR = grid$d)
  clim <- if (v == "TM") list(TM = grid$m, RR = zero) else list(TM = zero, RR = grid$m)
  X <- weather_design(model, dev, clim)
  Xc <- weather_design(model, dev, clim, capped = TRUE)
  grid %>%
    mutate(cell = sprintf("%+.2f (%.2f) / %+.2f", 100 * drop(X %*% model$coef),
                          100 * sqrt(rowSums((X %*% model$vcov) * X)), 100 * drop(Xc %*% model$coef)),
           m = paste(m, if (v == "TM") "C" else "m")) %>%
    select(d, m, cell) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = m, values_from = cell)
}
effect_grid("TM", c(-3, -1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8), c(5, 15, 25)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Growth effect that year (pp) of a temperature deviation of d SD at",
                               "long-run temperature m: estimate (SE) / capped"))
effect_grid("RR", c(-3, -2, -1, 1, 2, 3, 5), c(0.5, 1.5, 3)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Growth effect that year (pp) of a precipitation deviation of d SD at",
                               "long-run precipitation m (m a year): estimate (SE) / capped"))
```

# All scenarios

Every RCP and SAI setting (the 10 seeds of each together), uncapped and
capped, on `r WORKERS` R processes; the result is saved in
`results/sai_scenarios/` and reused while the model, the data, the settings and
the functions are unchanged.

```{r projections}
BASELINE <- params$baseline
MODEL_LABEL <- projection_label(model, BASELINE)
PROJECTIONS_FILE <- file.path("results", "sai_scenarios", paste0(
  "projections_", gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "_", tolower(paste(model$definition, model$form, BASELINE))),
  ".rds"))
scenario_file <- file.info(data_file(SCENARIO_FILE))
projections_spec <- list(
  model = model[c("suffix", "coef", "vcov", "moments", "support", "form_suffixes")],
  draws = draws, start = START, probs = PROBS, country_years = COUNTRY_YEARS,
  draw_step = as.integer(params$draw_step), trailing = c(TRAILING_YEARS, VARIABILITY_MIN_YEARS),
  baseline = BASELINE,
  scenario_file = c(size = scenario_file$size, modified = as.numeric(scenario_file$mtime)),
  code = code_fingerprint(project_all_scenarios, scenario_effects, scenario_deviations,
                          run_held_deviation, sigma_spell_held_deviation, fix_sigma_spells,
                          trailing_moments, grouped_trailing_moments,
                          gdp_loss, country_loss, weather_design, arm_value, arm_caps,
                          read_scenarios)
)
projections <- cached_result(PROJECTIONS_FILE, projections_spec, function() {
  project_all_scenarios(model, draws, start = START, country_years = COUNTRY_YEARS, probs = PROBS,
                        draw_step = as.integer(params$draw_step), scenarios = scenarios,
                        workers = WORKERS, baseline = BASELINE)
})
N_COUNTRIES <- length(unique(projections$country$region))
```

## How far the scenarios leave the estimation sample

```{r support}
projections$deviations %>%
  label_scenarios() %>%
  arrange(rcp_label, term_label, year) %>%
  transmute(RCP = rcp_label, SAI = term_label, year,
            across(T_median:P_p90, ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Deviations less those of natural variability alone (d - d_var, SDs) over the ", N_COUNTRIES,
    " countries and the 10 seeds: temperature median, 90th percentile and largest; precipitation ",
    "10th percentile, median and 90th percentile. Estimation sample: temperature ",
    round(min(model$support$TM), 2), " to ", round(max(model$support$TM), 2), ", precipitation ",
    round(min(model$support$RR), 2), " to ", round(max(model$support$RR), 2), " (demeaned)"))

projections$support %>%
  filter(!capped) %>%
  label_scenarios() %>%
  arrange(rcp_label, term_label) %>%
  transmute(RCP = rcp_label, SAI = term_label, across(c(hot, cold, wet, dry), ~ round(100 * .x, 1))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Country-years from ", START, " (%) with a deviation (with natural variability) beyond the ",
    "largest of the estimation sample on each side: where the capped variant differs"))
```

## Global GDP loss

```{r global-loss-table}
global_loss_table <- function(cap) {
  projections$global %>%
    filter(capped == cap, year %in% COUNTRY_YEARS) %>%
    label_scenarios() %>%
    mutate(cell = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]", 100 * central, 100 * low, 100 * high)) %>%
    select(rcp_label, term_label, year, cell) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = cell) %>%
    arrange(rcp_label, term_label) %>%
    rename(RCP = rcp_label, SAI = term_label) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
      "Global GDP loss (% of the scenarios' GDP, ", N_COUNTRIES, " countries; ", MODEL_LABEL,
      "), ", if (cap) "deviations capped at the sample support" else "model as estimated",
      ": median [", 100 * PROBS[1], "%, ", 100 * PROBS[3], "%] over the 10 seeds x ",
      params$n_draws, " coefficient draws; losses from ", START))
}
global_loss_table(FALSE)
global_loss_table(TRUE)
```

```{r global-loss-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=9}
for (cap in c(FALSE, TRUE)) {
  print(plot_scenarios(global_selection(projections, capped = cap, start = START, probs = PROBS,
                                        n_countries = N_COUNTRIES, model = model,
                                        baseline = BASELINE),
                       bands = c("BASE", "NOTERM")) +
          labs(title = paste("Global GDP loss,", if (cap) "deviations capped at the sample support"
                             else "model as estimated"),
               caption = paste("Line: median of the 10 seeds x", params$n_draws, "coefficient draws",
                               "(every", params$draw_step, "years); band: ", 100 * PROBS[1], "-",
                               100 * PROBS[3], "%, without SAI and SAI never terminated only, cut at",
                               "-100% if lower; thin lines: each seed (point estimate).")))
}
```

```{r global-temperature, fig.width=13, fig.height=9}
plot_scenarios(select_scenarios(rcp = names(SCENARIO_RCPS), term = SCENARIO_TERMS,
                                what = "temperature", regions = "WORLD"))
```

## Countries

```{r country-tables}
MAJOR <- c("USA", "CHN", "IND", "JPN", "DEU", "GBR", "FRA", "BRA", "RUS", "IDN", "MEX", "TUR",
           "SAU", "NGA", "EGY", "PAK", "BGD", "ETH", "COD", "ZAF")
country_table <- function(cap, year_shown = 2100L) {
  growth <- projections$country %>%
    filter(capped == cap, year == year_shown, rcp == "RCP45", term == "BASE") %>%
    select(region, g_base)
  projections$country %>%
    filter(capped == cap, year == year_shown, term %in% c("BASE", "NOTERM"), region %in% MAJOR) %>%
    mutate(column = paste(scenario_rcp_label(rcp), ifelse(term == "BASE", "no SAI", "SAI")),
           cell = sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", 100 * central, 100 * low, 100 * high)) %>%
    select(region, column, cell) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = cell) %>%
    left_join(growth, by = "region") %>%
    mutate(country = countrycode::countrycode(region, "iso3c", "country.name", warn = FALSE),
           growth = round(100 * g_base, 2)) %>%
    arrange(match(region, MAJOR)) %>%
    select(country, growth, starts_with("RCP")) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
      "GDP loss in ", year_shown, " (%, median [", 100 * PROBS[1], "%, ", 100 * PROBS[3], "%]), ",
      if (cap) "capped" else "as estimated", ", without SAI and with SAI never terminated; growth: ",
      "the scenarios' per-capita growth, mean ", START, "-2100 (% a year)"))
}
country_table(FALSE)
country_table(TRUE)

projections$country %>%
  filter(year %in% COUNTRY_YEARS) %>%
  group_by(rcp, term, capped, year) %>%
  summarise(gain = sum(central < 0), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(column = paste(year, ifelse(capped, "capped", "as estimated"))) %>%
  label_scenarios() %>%
  select(RCP = rcp_label, SAI = term_label, column, gain) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = gain) %>%
  arrange(RCP, SAI) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Countries whose median GDP change is a gain, of", N_COUNTRIES))

projections$country %>%
  filter(year == 2100L, term %in% c("BASE", "NOTERM")) %>%
  group_by(rcp, term, capped) %>%
  summarise(mean_growth_base = 100 * mean(g_base), mean_growth_climate = 100 * mean(g_cc),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  label_scenarios() %>%
  transmute(RCP = rcp_label, SAI = term_label, capped,
            across(starts_with("mean_"), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  arrange(RCP, SAI, capped) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Per-capita growth, mean over countries and ", START,
                                "-2100 (% a year): the scenarios', and with the climate (point ",
                                "estimate, mean over the seeds)"))
```

# Standardized or unstandardized deviations

The model above measures each year in SDs of the country's own variability.
The same model estimated on deviations in physical units (°C and metres a
year, not divided by the SD; "The preferred model without standardization" in
`weather_arms_robustness.Rmd`) fits the growth data as well: the difference in
fit cannot be told apart from noise. The losses it implies can still differ,
because the scenarios move the climate far more than a typical year does:

```text
standardized     d = (X - trailing 20-year mean) / SD       the same warming is a larger deviation where the SD is small
unstandardized   d =  X - trailing 20-year mean             the same warming is the same deviation everywhere (°C, m a year)
```

The unstandardized counterpart of the model (same definition and form, its
own coefficients) is projected in the same way: the same scenarios and seeds,
the same start, `r params$n_draws` draws of its coefficients, and the cap at
the largest deviation of its own estimation sample. With one variable
unstandardized at a time, the difference is attributed to temperature or to
precipitation.

```{r unstandardized-projections}
UNSTD_VARIANTS <- c("unstandardized" = paste0(params$definition, ", unstandardized"),
                    "T unstandardized" = paste0(params$definition, ", T unstandardized"),
                    "P unstandardized" = paste0(params$definition, ", P unstandardized"))
stopifnot(all(UNSTD_VARIANTS %in% names(readRDS(PREFERRED_MODEL_RDS)$models)))
# The projections of a saved model, saved and reused like the main ones.
project_model <- function(m) {
  m_draws <- coefficient_draws(m, n = as.integer(params$n_draws))
  file <- file.path("results", "sai_scenarios", paste0(
    "projections_", gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "_", tolower(paste(m$definition, m$form, BASELINE))),
    ".rds"))
  spec <- utils::modifyList(projections_spec, list(
    model = m[c("suffix", "coef", "vcov", "moments", "support", "form_suffixes")],
    draws = m_draws))
  cached_result(file, spec, function() {
    project_all_scenarios(m, m_draws, start = START, country_years = COUNTRY_YEARS, probs = PROBS,
                          draw_step = as.integer(params$draw_step), scenarios = scenarios,
                          workers = WORKERS, baseline = BASELINE)
  })
}
unstd_models <- lapply(UNSTD_VARIANTS, load_preferred_model, form = params$form)
runs <- c(list("standardized" = projections), lapply(unstd_models, project_model))

# 1. Global GDP loss, standardized and unstandardized (both variables).
global_cells <- bind_rows(lapply(names(runs), function(k) {
  runs[[k]]$global %>% filter(year %in% COUNTRY_YEARS) %>% mutate(model = k)
}))
standardization_table <- function(cap) {
  global_cells %>%
    filter(capped == cap, model %in% c("standardized", "unstandardized")) %>%
    label_scenarios() %>%
    mutate(cell = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]", 100 * central, 100 * low, 100 * high),
           column = paste(year, model)) %>%
    arrange(year, model) %>%
    select(RCP = rcp_label, SAI = term_label, column, cell) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = cell) %>%
    arrange(RCP, SAI) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
      "Global GDP loss (% of the scenarios' GDP, ", N_COUNTRIES, " countries), ",
      params$definition, " deviations, ", params$form, ", standardized (", MODEL_LABEL,
      ") and unstandardized, ", if (cap) "deviations capped at each model's sample support"
      else "models as estimated", ": median [", 100 * PROBS[1], "%, ", 100 * PROBS[3],
      "%] over the 10 seeds x ", params$n_draws, " coefficient draws; losses from ", START))
}
standardization_table(FALSE)
standardization_table(TRUE)

# 2. Which variable: the median loss with one variable unstandardized at a time.
global_cells %>%
  filter(!capped, year %in% c(2100L, 2150L)) %>%
  label_scenarios() %>%
  mutate(column = paste(year, model), median = round(100 * central, 1)) %>%
  arrange(year, match(model, names(runs))) %>%
  select(RCP = rcp_label, SAI = term_label, column, median) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = median) %>%
  arrange(RCP, SAI) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Global GDP loss (%, median, models as estimated) with both variables standardized, both ",
    "unstandardized, and one unstandardized at a time"))
```

```{r unstandardized-paths, fig.width=13, fig.height=8}
# 3. The paths of the global loss under both models.
PATH_TERMS <- c("BASE", "NOTERM", "2040", "2070", "2100")
bind_rows(lapply(c("standardized", "unstandardized"), function(k) {
  runs[[k]]$global %>% filter(!capped, term %in% PATH_TERMS) %>% mutate(model = k)
})) %>%
  label_scenarios() %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, 100 * central, colour = term_label, linetype = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~rcp_label, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = scenario_term_colours(), name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(standardized = "solid", unstandardized = "dashed"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Global GDP loss (%)",
       title = "Global GDP loss with standardized and unstandardized deviations",
       subtitle = paste0(params$definition, " deviations, ", params$form, ", models as estimated; ",
                         "median over the 10 seeds x ", params$n_draws, " coefficient draws.")) +
  theme_results()
```

```{r unstandardized-countries, fig.width=12, fig.height=5.5}
# 4. Countries: the loss in 2100 without SAI under both models, by long-run
# temperature and by the SD the standardized model divides by.
COUNTRY_CASES <- tibble::tribble(~rcp, ~term, "RCP45", "BASE", "RCP85", "BASE", "RCP85", "2070")
country_pairs <- bind_rows(lapply(c("standardized", "unstandardized"), function(k) {
  runs[[k]]$country %>%
    filter(!capped, year == 2100L) %>%
    inner_join(COUNTRY_CASES, by = c("rcp", "term")) %>%
    transmute(rcp, term, region, model = k, loss = 100 * central)
})) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = loss) %>%
  inner_join(select(model$moments, region = GID_0, mean_TM_all, sd_TM_lag_20), by = "region") %>%
  label_scenarios() %>%
  mutate(case = paste(rcp_label, term_label, sep = ", "),
         climate = cut(mean_TM_all, stats::quantile(unique(mean_TM_all), 0:3 / 3),
                       include.lowest = TRUE, labels = c("cold third", "mid third", "hot third")))

country_pairs %>%
  group_by(case, climate) %>%
  summarise(countries = n(), long_run_temperature = round(stats::median(mean_TM_all), 1),
            trailing_sd = round(stats::median(sd_TM_lag_20), 2),
            loss_standardized = round(stats::median(standardized), 1),
            loss_unstandardized = round(stats::median(unstandardized), 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(country_pairs %>%
              group_by(case) %>%
              summarise(rank_correlation = round(stats::cor(standardized, unstandardized,
                                                            method = "spearman"), 2)),
            by = "case") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Countries by third of long-run temperature: median long-run temperature (°C), median ",
    "trailing 20-year SD of temperature (°C, the SD the standardized model divides by), and ",
    "the median GDP loss in 2100 (%, models as estimated) under each model; rank correlation ",
    "of the two losses across the countries of the scenario"))

ggplot(country_pairs, aes(standardized, unstandardized, colour = mean_TM_all)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8, alpha = 0.85) +
  facet_wrap(~case, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_gradient(low = "#b8d4f5", high = "#0d3f7a", name = "Long-run temperature (°C)") +
  labs(x = "GDP loss in 2100, standardized deviations (%)",
       y = "GDP loss in 2100, unstandardized deviations (%)",
       title = "Country losses in 2100 with standardized and unstandardized deviations",
       subtitle = "Median over the seeds and draws, models as estimated; line: equal losses.") +
  theme_results() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "#e6e5df", linewidth = 0.3))

# 5. How far each model is taken beyond its estimation sample.
bind_rows(lapply(c("standardized", "unstandardized"), function(k) {
  runs[[k]]$support %>% filter(!capped) %>% mutate(model = k)
})) %>%
  inner_join(tibble::tibble(rcp = c("RCP45", "RCP45", "RCP85", "RCP85", "RCP85"),
                            term = c("BASE", "NOTERM", "BASE", "NOTERM", "2070")),
             by = c("rcp", "term")) %>%
  label_scenarios() %>%
  arrange(rcp_label, term_label, model) %>%
  transmute(RCP = rcp_label, SAI = term_label, model,
            across(c(hot, cold, wet, dry), ~ round(100 * .x, 1))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Country-years from ", START, " (%) with a deviation beyond the largest of the model's own ",
    "estimation sample, on each side (where the capped variant differs)"))
```

# Selecting a scenario

`select_scenarios()` reads the scenarios of the given RCPs and SAI settings
(`rcp`: "RCP3PD", "RCP45", "RCP6", "RCP85"; `term`: "BASE", "NOTERM" or a
termination year; `seed`: NULL for all ten), and returns, for the countries
`regions` (NULL: all; ISO3 codes; "WORLD" for the model's global temperature):

- `what = "gdp_loss"`: the GDP loss from `start` (pooled median and band, and
  each seed), as estimated or `capped`;
- `what = "temperature"` or `"precipitation"`: each seed's series
  (population-weighted over the countries), and the seed mean without natural
  variability.

`plot_scenarios()` plots a selection, or takes the same arguments directly.

```{r example-loss, fig.width=12, fig.height=5.5}
plot_scenarios(rcp = c("RCP45", "RCP85"), term = c("BASE", "NOTERM", "2050", "2080"),
               what = "gdp_loss", capped = TRUE, model = model, draws = draws,
               baseline = BASELINE)
```

```{r example-subset, fig.width=12, fig.height=5.5}
south_asia <- select_scenarios(rcp = c("RCP45", "RCP85"), term = c("BASE", "NOTERM", "2070"),
                               regions = c("IND", "PAK", "BGD", "NPL", "LKA"), model = model,
                               draws = draws, baseline = BASELINE)
plot_scenarios(south_asia)
south_asia$summary %>%
  filter(year %in% COUNTRY_YEARS) %>%
  transmute(RCP = rcp_label, SAI = term_label, year,
            across(c(low, value, high), ~ round(100 * .x, 1))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "South Asia: GDP loss (%), as estimated")
```

```{r example-climate, fig.width=12, fig.height=5.5}
plot_scenarios(rcp = c("RCP45", "RCP85"), term = c("BASE", "NOTERM", "2070"),
               what = "temperature", regions = c("IND", "PAK", "BGD", "NPL", "LKA"))
plot_scenarios(rcp = c("RCP45", "RCP85"), term = c("BASE", "NOTERM", "2070"),
               what = "precipitation", regions = "IND")
```
